newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel dives, jet trades at $22.10.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel dives, jet trades at $22.10.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market nosedived on jitters that regional demand has almost come to a standstill, while jet fuel's freefall was curbed by a purchase at $22.10 per barrel, traders said on Wednesday.
The freefall was triggered on the gas oil swaps market when a major offered at low levels and followed by almost every other trading company.

The major offered down the physical market even lower at $148 per tonne ($19.80 per barrel) for second-half July lifting free-on-board (fob) basis. Four other offers were seen, involving three traders and another major, between $20.00 and $20.40 per barrel.

The $19.80-level was the lowest in at least three years, but the near term bottom was still not in sight, as buyers remained absent because they did not see any regional demand to soak up their purchases, traders said.
The biggest stumbling block was China's absence from the market for the third quarter, which was also used as an excuse to sell down the swaps market earlier in the day, traders said.

Current rock bottom gas oil values were in stark contrast to levels seen only three months ago when a buying frenzy by a group of traders led by a Singapore trading company bought a record 18 million tonnes with prices hitting a high of $28.30 during late March.

Traders said the major who was the most aggressive seller on both the physical and swaps market could be under pressure to sell their excess barrels despite cutting runs at their refinery to an average 49,000 tonnes per day in July.
They said other refiners need to follow suit to help mop out excess supplies and curb a further freefall which has eroded refining profit margins.
Traders said a Singapore trader recently bought a 30,000-40,000 tonnes cargo on an fob Okinawa basis at a 40-cent discount but the Japanese trader who was said to be the seller denied the sale.
Traders said a U.S. trader sold a jet fuel cargo for July 24-28 lifting to a Singapore trader at $22.10 per barrel, which they said was a good price considering the current bearish mood.
The U.S. trader was earlier offering at $21.85 per barrel.
August jet fuel swaps traded earlier at $23.00 per barrel.
Sri Lanka will decide on Tuesday to whther to issue a gas oil/jet fuel tender for early August delivery, a source in Colombo said.
